Hi all — attaching the sample CSV and an extract spec. Notes below.

Attachment: who_when_sample.csv (text/csv, 6KB)
Attachment: extract-spec.md (text/markdown, 4KB)

Sample columns (what we'll include by default):
- actor_id (string) — internal user id; can be hashed with HMAC-SHA256 using a customer key for pseudonymization
- actor_role (string) — role at time of request (end-user, admin, service)
- request_id (string) — unique per API call
- model_version (string) — model identifier serving the request
- action (string) — e.g., generate, embed, prompt_edit
- resource_path (string) — object accessed (conversation id / document id)
- source_ip (ip_address) — optional; can be redacted
- timestamp_utc (ISO8601) — event time in UTC (we include TZ-normalized timestamps)
- kv_cache_hit (boolean) — whether response used cached KV at runtime

Timezone and timestamps: we normalize all events to UTC in the export (timestamp_utc) and include an optional local_timestamp column on request when requested. All timestamps are ISO8601 (RFC3339).

Pseudonymization options:
- HMAC-SHA256 with customer-provided key (recommended). We store only the hashed value in the export; original mapping is not exported.
- IP redaction: we can strip last octet, blank IPs entirely, or provide full IP with contract-level security controls.

Retention and residency:
- Default: 90 days for access logs and request-level traces.
- Configurable: 30 days (min), 180 days, or up to 7 years under enterprise contract.
- Residency: logs can be retained and exported from a US-only region (us-east1). For on-prem/private, logs remain in-customer VPC.

Delivery/exports:
- Scheduled export to SFTP (key-based) or signed Drive folder (authenticated link)
- On-demand CSV/JSON downloadable via our secure admin console (HTTPS, short-lived link)
- We can also push to a customer-owned S3 bucket with presigned URLs (enterprise).

SLAs: periodic exports (daily) are included; expedited exports (ad-hoc, within 24 hours) available under enterprise SLA. For audit evidence requests requiring certified attestation, we offer a signed letter (on Redwood letterhead) describing the export process and controls.

Next step: Emma — can you confirm whether Brightline requires full IPs, hashed user identifiers, or neither, and whether the auditors need local timestamps?

Thanks,
Rishi Malhotra
